docs.title: YeetnGreet docs
docs.text:
YeetnGreet helps IT admins onboard and offboard Microsoft 365 users from a Windows PC — without putting tenant data in our cloud.

Microsoft Graph runs on your technicians’ machines. We only use the cloud for your YeetnGreet license and billing. YeetnGreet is proprietary software.

docs.title: What counts as a licensed user
docs.text:
A licensed user is an enabled account that has at least one paid Microsoft 365 license.

Do not count:

  • Trial, developer, or free licenses
  • Disabled accounts
  • Shared mailboxes

docs.text: YeetnGreet is built so customer Microsoft 365 data stays between your technicians and the tenant they are working in — not in our cloud.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Need help with YeetnGreet? Start with the docs, then email us. This page is for IT admins running the Windows app against Microsoft 365 tenants.

docs.title: How to get help
docs.text:
Email support@yeetngreet.app.

That is the public support address. Please do not open GitHub Issues for product support — the application repository is private, and Issues are not a customer support channel. YeetnGreet is proprietary software.

docs.title: Check the docs first
docs.text:
Many how-tos are already covered here:

Topic Docs Install and launch Install First tenant sign-in and preview First run Offboard / onboard / schedules Jobs License and unused-license reports Reports Switching tenants Multi-tenant Plans and limits Pricing and licensing What we store Privacy

If the docs answer it, you save a round-trip — and we can spend support time on the harder cases.

docs.title: What to include in your email
docs.text:
The more context you send up front, the faster we can help. Please include:

  1. App version — Help → About in YeetnGreet (or the version shown on the About screen)
  2. Windows version — for example Windows 11 23H2, or winver output
  3. Plan — Free, Starter, Growth, Business, Scale, Large, or Enterprise
  4. Tenant domain — the Microsoft 365 domain you were working in (for example contoso.com), not passwords or secrets
  5. Steps to reproduce — what you clicked or ran, what you expected, and what happened
  6. Screenshots — if the issue is in the UI (redact PII where you can)

Do not send secrets

Do not include passwords, refresh tokens, client secrets, or full mailbox contents. Tenant domain and a short error message are enough for most Graph failures.

docs.title: Response expectations
docs.text:
We monitor support@yeetngreet.app and reply on business days. Timing varies with volume and how much detail is in the initial email — we do not publish a formal SLA here.

Urgent production blockers still go to the same address; put a clear subject line (for example Offboard blocked — Graph 403) so we can prioritize.

docs.title: First run
docs.text: After install, walk through a low-risk path: pick a tenant, confirm it's the right one, then preview before anything runs.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
1. Launch YeetnGreet on your PC
  2. Sign in to your Microsoft 365 tenant on Tenants. Admin consent must already be granted in that tenant. See Admin permissions and consent
  3. Confirm the tenant name and domain are the ones you expect
  4. Open Offboard or Onboard and click Preview before you confirm
  5. Optionally save a template if this tenant has a standard checklist

Preview lists every planned action and changes nothing.

Confirm the tenant

Say the organization name out loud before you confirm. Running a job in the wrong tenant is expensive. The tenant picker at the top of the left rail shows which tenant every job runs in. See Multi-tenant.

docs.title: Suggested first job
docs.text: Goal Path Practice offboard flow Offboard with a test user or dry-run style preview Practice onboard flow Onboard creating a clearly labeled test account See license value License audit on a tenant you know well

docs.title: Where local files live
docs.text: Working files (templates, local logs, and related data) stay on your PC, typically under AppData or Documents — unless you choose another location. They are not uploaded to YeetnGreet’s cloud as job payloads.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: YeetnGreet is a Windows app that uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 for the UI. Each technician installs it on their own Windows PC with YeetnGreet-Setup.exe.

docs.title: 1. Get the setup file
docs.text:
Public Windows downloads are not available yet. When your access is ready:

  1. Join the waitlist on the pricing page
  2. Run YeetnGreet-Setup.exe on each technician PC that will use YeetnGreet

Coming with the release

The setup file ships with the release for licensed users. Waitlist members get access through the preregister path first. Download links will appear here when the public release ships.

docs.title: 2. Install
docs.text:
1. Double-click YeetnGreet-Setup.exe
  2. Allow Windows SmartScreen / firewall prompts if your environment shows them
  3. The setup installs for the current user — no admin rights required
  4. Files go under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\YeetnGreet
  5. Windows gets a Start menu shortcut and an uninstall entry in Settings
  6. You can delete the setup file after install

docs.title: 3. WebView2
docs.text:
Most Windows 10/11 machines already have the Evergreen WebView2 Runtime. If the app cannot start the UI:

  1. Install (or repair) the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime
  2. Open YeetnGreet again from the Start menu

docs.title: 4. First launch
docs.text:
1. Open YeetnGreet from the Start menu
  2. You should see the YeetnGreet shell ready for tenant sign-in

First launch: the app opens on Offboard. Sign in to your YeetnGreet profile from the account menu, then pick a tenant.

docs.title: 5. Tenant sign-in
docs.text:
Sign in with an account that can administer the Microsoft 365 tenant you are working in. Graph calls leave from this PC to Microsoft — not through YeetnGreet’s vendor cloud.

Admin consent first

Each tenant needs an admin to grant consent for YeetnGreet's Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online permissions before the first job. See Admin permissions and consent for the full list.

After Microsoft sign-in on this PC, the Tenants page confirms which tenant and account you are signed in to.

What our cloud sees

License and billing metadata for your YeetnGreet account only. Not mail, files, or directory content used during jobs.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: YeetnGreet updates itself in place. You do not need to keep YeetnGreet-Setup.exe on disk or re-run setup for routine updates.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
To remove YeetnGreet from a PC:

  1. Open Windows Settings → Apps, or use the Uninstall YeetnGreet Start menu shortcut
  2. Follow the uninstall prompts
  3. The uninstaller asks whether to also delete logs and reports in Documents\YeetnGreet. Shared/central log folders are never deleted. Tenant settings in %LOCALAPPDATA%\YeetnGreet are kept unless you remove that folder.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with First run to complete a safe preview job.

docs.title: Admin permissions and consent
docs.text:
YeetnGreet changes users, mailboxes, licenses, and devices in your Microsoft 365 tenant. Microsoft requires an administrator in each tenant you manage to approve (grant admin consent for) the permissions below before YeetnGreet can run jobs there.

Use this page as the checklist for your Global Administrator, or for your own change ticket.

Not the same as YeetnGreet roles

This page is about Microsoft 365 permissions in each tenant. Who can edit templates and tenants inside YeetnGreet is set by YeetnGreet's own Admin and Tech roles.

Admin consent is per tenant

Consent granted in one tenant does not carry over to another. If you manage more than one tenant, repeat it for every tenant you add to YeetnGreet. Granting admin consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions needs a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator in that tenant.

docs.title: How YeetnGreet signs in
docs.text:
Sign-in mode What runs the job What your admin approves App-only (needed for scheduled jobs) Your own app registration in this tenant, signing in with a certificate key that stays on the technician's PC. No admin account is signed in. The application permissions and roles below, on your app registration Interactive An admin signs in to the tenant in the browser The delegated permissions below, plus admin roles on the admin's account

Either way, tokens are requested for the tenant you selected. YeetnGreet refuses to run a job if Microsoft returns a token for a different tenant.

docs.title: App-only: your own app in each tenant
docs.text:
YeetnGreet LLC doesn't own an app or hold a key for your tenant, and there's no shared YeetnGreet app to consent to. For app-only, each tenant gets its own single-tenant app registration, created in that tenant, and the technician's PC holds its own certificate key for it. One key can only ever open one tenant.

  1. In the tenant: Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration. Supported account types: Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant). No redirect URI and no client secret.
  2. Add the application permissions below and grant admin consent. Add the roles below.
  3. In YeetnGreet: Tenants → select the tenant → App-only for scheduled jobs → paste the app's Application (client) ID → Create key on this PC.
  4. Upload the .cer file YeetnGreet saved to the app registration (Certificates & secrets → Certificates → Upload certificate), then click Save in YeetnGreet.

About the key:

  • It's created on the technician's PC and can't be exported: in the PC's TPM chip when it has one, otherwise in Windows key storage with export turned off. Only the public certificate (.cer) leaves the PC.
  • It's valid for 12 months at most. YeetnGreet warns 30 days before it expires.
  • Any other key is blocked, not just flagged. If a certificate's private key can be exported, or the certificate is valid for more than 12 months, YeetnGreet won't save it and scheduled jobs won't sign in with it. The Tenants page shows the key as Blocked. Create a new key with Create key on this PC, upload its .cer, and click Save. The 30-day expiry notice is only a warning: jobs keep running until the key expires.
  • Client secrets and PFX files aren't supported. Each PC that runs scheduled jobs creates its own key.

Rotating the key

  1. Create new key on the Tenants page and upload the new .cer to the same app registration (keep the old one for now).
  2. Click Save in YeetnGreet to switch to the new key, and check the next job signs in.
  3. Delete the old certificate from the app registration, then Delete old key in YeetnGreet.

If a PC is lost, delete its certificate from the app registration straight away. That alone stops the key working.

docs.title: App-only: application permissions
docs.text: Grant these on your app registration in this tenant (App registrations → your app → API permissions → Grant admin consent). All are Application permissions.

docs.title: Microsoft Graph
docs.text:
Permission Why YeetnGreet needs it User.ReadWrite.All Create onboard accounts and update user details: manager, usage location, address-list visibility, and moving direct reports to a new manager. User.EnableDisableAccount.All Block sign-in for leavers and enable new hires' accounts. User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All Reset the leaver's password and set the new hire's first password. User.RevokeSessions.All Sign the leaver out of every active session. UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All Remove the leaver's MFA methods: Authenticator, phone, FIDO2, Windows Hello, software OATH, and email. LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All Assign licenses at onboard, remove them at offboard, and read license SKUs for the license audit. GroupMember.ReadWrite.All Add new hires to groups and remove leavers from groups. RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory Optional — leave it out unless you need it. Remove Entra admin role assignments from leavers. Only needed if you use Remove Entra directory roles. Without it, the app greys out that action and the job reports the step as Skipped. Directory.Read.All Read-only: tenant details, verified domains, and group and role memberships. YeetnGreet never writes with this permission. MailboxSettings.ReadWrite Set the leaver's out-of-office auto-reply. Files.ReadWrite.All Share the leaver's OneDrive with their manager or the handoff person. DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All Find the leaver's Intune-managed devices (read only). Only needed if you use Retire Intune devices. DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All Optional. Retire those Intune devices. Requires admin consent. Without consent, the app greys out Retire. Only needed if you use Retire Intune devices. Reports.Read.All Read Microsoft 365 mail activity for the Unused licenses and License audit reports.

YeetnGreet does not request application Mail.Send. Report email delivery is interactive-only (see below).

Why role removal is optional

RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory can assign any Entra role, including Global Administrator. YeetnGreet only uses it to remove admin roles from leavers, so you can leave it out. If it isn't granted, Remove Entra directory roles is greyed out with a short explanation, and offboarding jobs (including scheduled and batch jobs) skip that step and report it as Skipped, not failed. Remove the leaver's admin roles in the Entra admin center instead.

docs.title: Office 365 Exchange Online
docs.text: Permission Why YeetnGreet needs it Exchange.ManageAsApp Connect to Exchange Online without a user, so YeetnGreet can convert the leaver's mailbox to shared, grant Full Access to the handoff person, and hide the mailbox from the address list.

docs.title: Roles for your app registration
docs.text:
Microsoft requires a role on the app as well as the permissions above for some actions. Give it the smallest ones:

Role Why User Administrator (Entra role) Microsoft requires at least this role for an app to reset passwords. Assign it in Entra admin center → Roles & admins → User Administrator → Add assignments → your app. A custom Exchange role group with Mail Recipients, Distribution Groups and Security Group Creation and Membership (recommended), or the Exchange Recipient Administrator Entra role Exchange Online only accepts Exchange.ManageAsApp when the app also holds an Exchange role. These cover the mailbox steps: convert to shared, Full Access, hide from the address list, and remove the leaver from distribution lists. A custom role group can also be limited to some mailboxes.

Don't give the app Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator. Neither is needed.

Offboarding an admin

Microsoft blocks lower-privileged roles from disabling, resetting, or removing MFA for other administrators. If you offboard someone who holds an admin role, the app may need Privileged Authentication Administrator. Otherwise, do those steps in the Entra admin center.

docs.title: Keeping app-only safe
docs.text:
• Limit where the app can sign in from. Conditional Access for workload identities can block the app's sign-ins from anywhere except your technicians' office IP addresses. It needs Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium, and it works for single-tenant apps like this one.
  • Watch its sign-ins. Entra admin center → Sign-in logs → Service principal sign-ins, filtered by the app's client ID. Alert on sign-ins from IP addresses you don't know.
  • Alert on changes. Watch the audit log for new certificates or secrets on the app, new API permissions or consent, and the app being added to a role. If you didn't plan the change, treat it as an incident.
  • Turn it off fast. Entra admin center → Enterprise applications → your app → Properties → Enabled for users to sign in? → No. That stops new sign-ins at once. Then delete its certificate from the app registration.

docs.title: Interactive: delegated permissions
docs.text:
When an admin signs in, YeetnGreet requests these delegated Microsoft Graph permissions.

Required:

User.ReadWrite.All, User.EnableDisableAccount.All, User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All, User.Read (your organization's verified domains), User.RevokeSessions.All, LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All, UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, GroupMember.ReadWrite.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, Reports.Read.All

Optional (each turns on one feature; without it, sign-in still works and that feature is greyed out):

Permission Feature DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All and DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All Retire Intune devices Mail.Send Report email delivery RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory Remove Entra directory roles from leavers

If your tenant hasn't consented to the optional permissions, YeetnGreet signs in with the required ones only and shows one note listing what's missing.

Interactive sign-in uses Microsoft's Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools app. The first time, approve the consent prompt and tick Consent on behalf of your organization, or grant admin consent to that app in your tenant.

Consent alone doesn't let an admin run the job. The signed-in account needs an active admin role too:

Role on the signed-in account Why User Administrator (or Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator) Required to disable accounts and reset passwords. YeetnGreet checks for it when it can read your roles and stops before a Live job if it's missing. Exchange Administrator Needed for the Exchange Online sign-in that runs the mailbox steps.

Report email delivery

Sending a report by email uses delegated Mail.Send and works only in interactive sign-in. In app-only mode, email delivery is unavailable — use a webhook or save the report locally instead. Application Mail.Send is not used.

docs.title: What YeetnGreet does not need
docs.text:
• Broad directory write or site-wide access: YeetnGreet doesn't request Directory.ReadWrite.All, Directory.AccessAsUser.All, Sites.FullControl.All, or DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All. Each step uses the narrowest permission Microsoft offers for it.
  • Access beyond your work account to use YeetnGreet itself: signing in to YeetnGreet for team and license features only uses User.Read against your own work account. It never grants access to your tenant's data.
  • On-premises Active Directory: YeetnGreet works with cloud-only Microsoft 365 (Entra ID). On-premises and hybrid Active Directory aren't supported yet.
  • Application Mail.Send: not requested. Email reports are interactive-only (delegated Mail.Send).

docs.title: Checklist for each tenant
docs.text:
1. Grant admin consent for every Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online permission above
  2. App-only: create a single-tenant app registration in the tenant, give it User Administrator and the Exchange role group (or Exchange Recipient Administrator), then create its key in YeetnGreet and upload the .cer
  3. Interactive: confirm the signed-in admin account has User Administrator (or higher) and Exchange Administrator
  4. If you use Retire Intune devices: confirm admin consent for DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All and DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All (otherwise Retire stays greyed out)
  5. If you use Remove Entra directory roles: confirm admin consent for RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory (otherwise that action stays greyed out and is skipped)
  6. Run a Preview in First run before any Live job

Updating from an earlier version

Grant consent for the new permissions first (Directory.Read.All and DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All for app-only; User.Read and DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All for interactive), then remove the old ones. Removing a permission from the app doesn't take back consent your tenant already gave, so remove Directory.ReadWrite.All, Sites.FullControl.All, Directory.AccessAsUser.All, and DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All in Enterprise applications → Permissions (on your app-only app registration, and on Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools for interactive) once the new set works. If you set up app-only with an earlier version, move to one single-tenant app per tenant with a key created in YeetnGreet, remove the Exchange Administrator role from the app, and delete any old client secrets and certificates from it.

docs.title: Roles: admin and tech
docs.text:
YeetnGreet has two roles for the people who use the app: Admin and Tech. Your role decides what you can change in YeetnGreet itself, such as templates, the tenant list, and where logs go.

Roles are not Microsoft 365 admin permissions

This page covers YeetnGreet's own roles. They don't give anyone rights in a Microsoft 365 tenant. What a job can change in a tenant still depends on the admin consent and the Entra roles described in Admin permissions and consent. A Tech still signs in to the tenant with an account that has the right Microsoft roles.

docs.title: Two different sign-ins
docs.text:
Sign-in Where What it's for YeetnGreet profile Account menu at the bottom of the left rail, or Settings → Profile Your plan, your role, and your company's shared tenants and templates. Uses only User.Read on your own work account. Tenant sign-in Tenants page Running jobs and reports in a Microsoft 365 tenant.

Your role comes from your YeetnGreet profile, so sign in to the profile to get it.

docs.title: What each role can do
docs.text:
Task Admin Tech Run offboard, onboard, and mover jobs Yes Yes, with an applied template Schedule jobs Yes Yes, with an applied template Run license reports and use What-if Yes Yes Review templates and apply them to jobs Yes Yes Create, update, delete, and publish templates Yes No Set or clear a tenant's default templates Yes No Add, edit, or remove tenants Yes No Invite operators and change their role on the Admin page Yes No Set the central logs folder on the Admin page Yes No

Your role shows under your name in the account menu: Admin or Tech. Click Sign Out in the same menu to sign out of your YeetnGreet profile.

Left: an admin's account menu, with the Admin page one click away. Right: a Tech's menu, with no Admin entry.

docs.title: Who gets which role
docs.text:
• The license owner is the first admin. Only the person who signs in with the email on your license becomes an admin automatically. Being the first person to sign in doesn't make you an admin.
  • Everyone else joins as Tech. A coworker who signs in to the YeetnGreet profile with a work account on your company's email domain joins as a Tech, as long as the org has room for another licensed user.
  • Admins invite operators and set roles. An admin can invite people and promote or demote them on the Admin page. See Invite operators and change roles.

On the Free plan there are no roles. Whoever uses the app on that PC can do everything, and templates are optional.

docs.title: Set up roles
docs.text:
1. Owner signs in first. On the PC of the person whose email is on the license, open the account menu and click Sign in. Use the license email. The account menu then shows Admin under the name.
  2. Add the tenants. On Tenants, add each tenant your team works in. Admins can change this list.
  3. Build and publish templates. On Templates, create the offboard, onboard, and mover templates for each tenant, then click Publish on each one. Optionally click Set as default. See Templates.
  4. Invite your team (optional). Open the account menu, click Admin, and invite each Tech under Operators. See below.
  5. Set the logs folder (optional). On the Admin page, enter a shared folder or UNC path under Central logs, then click Save logs path. Techs write their logs there and can't change it.
  6. Techs sign in. Each Tech installs YeetnGreet, opens the account menu, and signs in to the YeetnGreet profile with their work account. Their PC pulls your tenants and published templates automatically.

docs.title: Invite operators and change roles
docs.text:
Open the account menu and click Admin. The Operators card lists everyone who can use YeetnGreet for your company, with their role. Invited people who haven't signed in yet are marked invited.

To Do this Invite someone Click Invite…, enter their work Microsoft UPN, pick tech or admin, and click Invite. They get the role the first time they sign in to the YeetnGreet profile. Make a Tech an admin Click Make admin next to their name. Make an admin a Tech Click Make tech next to their name. Remove someone Click Remove next to their name. This also revokes their access to your YeetnGreet org. To let them back in, invite them again. See the latest list Click Refresh.

Your org always keeps at least one admin, so Make tech and Remove are greyed out for the last admin. Invites count toward your plan's licensed users. When the org is full, YeetnGreet refuses the invite, or a role change that needs another licensed user, and tells you the plan's licensed users are full. Remove someone or move to a larger plan first.

The Admin page. Operators lists your admins and Techs; one invite is waiting for its first sign-in.

Invite with the person's own work account, not the account they use to sign in to a customer tenant.

docs.title: The Tech template lock
docs.text:
On paid plans, a Tech's jobs always follow a company template. A Tech fills in who the job is for. The template decides what the job does.

Job A Tech can fill in Locked to the template Offboard The people leaving, the handoff recipient, and the manager Every action and the auto-reply text Onboard Name, UPN, and manager, plus any job, organization, or contact field the template leaves blank The actions, the groups, the licenses, and every field the template sets, such as a department Mover The person who is moving, plus any new-position field the template leaves blank The actions, the groups, the licenses, and every new-position field the template sets
  • A template is required. Offboard, Onboard, and Mover show Template (required). Preview and Run stay locked until a template is applied.
  • Fields the template sets are locked. When a template sets a field, such as an onboard department of Sales, the job uses that value and a Tech can't change it. The field is greyed out with a dashed border, and its label ends in · template. Hover over it to see Set by company template. This includes the usage location when the template sets one.
  • Fields the template leaves blank are yours. A Tech can fill in a field the template doesn't set, such as a job title, and the job keeps that value.
  • Required fields must be filled. If the template marks a field as required, the job won't run until it's filled in.
  • Groups and licenses come only from the template. A Tech can't add groups or licenses, or remove the ones the template adds.
  • The lock is checked again when the job runs. YeetnGreet applies the template's actions, groups, and licenses again when it runs the job, so changes made outside the job page don't carry through. Scheduled jobs are checked when you schedule them.
  • Techs can't change templates. They can review a template on Templates and apply it to a job. Only admins create, edit, publish, or set defaults.

A Tech fills in who the new hire is, including the job title this template leaves blank. Fields marked · template, the actions, the groups, and the license come from the template.

A Tech can review a template and apply it, but not change it.

Techs apply a template before they can preview or run an offboard.

docs.title: What a Tech sees
docs.text:
• Templates is review-only. A note at the top says templates come from your admin. The editor is greyed out, and only Apply to job is available.
  • Offboard, Onboard, and Mover show Template (required), and the locked settings are greyed out.
  • Tenants lists your company's tenants, but adding or editing them is locked.
  • The account menu shows Tech under your name and has no Admin entry.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Sign in to the YeetnGreet profile first. On paid plans, tenant names stay hidden until you're signed in to the profile.
  • Owner signs in first. Only the license email becomes an admin on its own. Until the owner signs in, nobody can invite operators or change roles.
  • Invite the work account. Use the person's own work Microsoft account, not a customer tenant admin account.
  • Techs need a published template. If a template exists only on the admin's PC, the Tech gets "Template not found locally." Publish it, then the Tech can open Settings → Profile → Refresh company catalog.
  • Role changes apply at the next sign-in. After you change someone's role, they see it the next time they sign in to the YeetnGreet profile.
  • Role isn't access to the tenant. An admin in YeetnGreet still needs the right Microsoft 365 roles to sign in to a tenant and run a job.

docs.title: Offboard
docs.text: Offboard one person or many. Use templates for handoff, checklist, and shared settings. Preview what will run, confirm deliberately, then go — or schedule the job for later on the same PC.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You are signed into the correct customer tenant
  • You have the leaver’s identity (UPN / email) or a CSV for batch
  • You know where mail / OneDrive / ownership should hand off

docs.title: 1. Open Offboard and select users
docs.text:
Choose a single user, multi-select from a list, or import a CSV.

Search by name or UPN to add people to the batch; the applied template sets the actions.

docs.title: 2. Apply template, handoff, and checklist
docs.text:
• Templates capture repeatable offboard settings for a tenant. See Templates
  • Handoff routes mailbox / content ownership as your process requires
  • Checklist items keep the human steps visible next to the automation

docs.title: 3. Preview
docs.text:
Review the planned actions. Fix anything wrong before confirm.

Preview is a dry run: it lists the planned actions for the batch and changes nothing. Type CONFIRM, then run.

docs.title: 4. Type-to-confirm
docs.text: YeetnGreet asks for a deliberate confirmation (type-to-confirm) so Live offboards are hard to trigger by accident.

docs.title: 5. Run now or schedule
docs.text:
• Run now — executes on this technician PC
  • Schedule — queues for a later time on this same PC (the machine must be on and signed in as required). See Schedules.

docs.title: Batch tips
docs.text:
Tip Why Validate CSV columns first Bad UPNs fail loudly mid-batch Use one template per customer standard Keeps handoff and checklist consistent Preview a single row before full CSV Catches tenant / license surprises early

Live means Live

After confirm, Graph changes happen in the customer tenant from this PC. Double-check tenant and users.

docs.title: Onboard
docs.text: Create or enable Microsoft 365 users, optionally assign licenses, groups, and a manager, then unlock Live work with an explicit CONFIRM.

docs.title: Before you start

  • Which SKUs, groups, and manager apply (or a saved template)

docs.title: 1. Open Onboard
docs.text:
Create a new account or enable an existing one. You can require a password change on first sign-in when your process calls for it.

A template fills groups, licenses, and required fields; you add the person's name, UPN, and manager.

docs.title: 2. Optional assignments
docs.text: Option Typical use Licenses Assign the right SKUs up front Groups Security / M365 groups for access Manager Org hierarchy and approval routing

docs.title: 3. Templates and CSV
docs.text:
• Templates — repeatable onboard defaults per tenant. See Templates
  • CSV — bulk create/enable with the same confirm path

docs.title: 4. CONFIRM
docs.text: Type CONFIRM (or the app’s required confirmation text) to unlock Live onboard. Preview first when the UI offers it.

docs.title: 5. Run or schedule
docs.text:
Same model as offboard: run immediately on this PC, or schedule for later on this PC.

Test accounts

For practice, use a clearly labeled test UPN and remove it when done — especially on production tenants.

docs.title: Schedules
docs.text: Schedule onboard, offboard, and report jobs to run later on the same technician PC where you created them.

docs.title: How scheduling works
docs.text:
1. Build the job as usual (users, template, delivery options)
  2. Choose a future run time instead of Run now
  3. Leave the PC able to run YeetnGreet at that time (powered on, user session / auth as your process requires)

Scheduled jobs on this PC: one-time offboard and onboard runs plus recurring license reports, each with Run now and Cancel.

Schedules are local to the PC

A scheduled job does not run in YeetnGreet’s cloud. If the PC is off or YeetnGreet cannot run, the job will not execute until conditions allow — plan cutovers accordingly.

docs.title: Good uses
docs.text:
• Friday evening offboards after payroll clears
  • Monday morning onboard batches
  • Weekly license or unused licenses reports with delivery

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
A template is a saved set of job settings for one tenant. You pick it on Offboard, Onboard, or Mover, click Apply, and the job uses those settings. Templates keep every technician on the same checklist for that tenant.

There are three kinds:

Kind What it sets Offboard Which offboard actions run, plus the default auto-reply message Onboard Optional onboard steps, default usage location, extra required fields, default groups and licenses Mover Mover steps, the default new position (job title, department, company, office, employee type), and groups and licenses to add

Templates belong to the tenant selected in the left rail. A template you save for Contoso doesn't show up for Fabrikam.

Who can edit templates

Admins create, edit, delete, and publish templates and set defaults. Techs can open a template to review it and apply it to a job, but they can't change it. On a Tech's job page the template's actions, groups, and licenses are locked, and the Tech fills in who the job is for. See The Tech template lock.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Select the tenant in the left rail.
  • Sign in to the tenant on Tenants if you want to search live groups and licenses for an onboard or mover template. Actions and text fields work without signing in.
  • On a paid plan, sign in to your YeetnGreet profile from the account menu so you can publish templates for the rest of your team.

docs.title: Create an offboard template
docs.text:
1. Open Templates and click Offboard.
  2. Click New. The editor resets to the default actions.
  3. Tick the actions this tenant's leavers should get. These always run and can't be turned off: temporary password, revoke sessions, and reset MFA.
  4. Write the Default auto-reply message. You can use these tokens, which are filled in for each person at run time: {{DisplayName}}, {{ManagerUpn}}, {{ManagerDisplayName}}, {{Upn}}.
  5. Click Save as new…, type a name, and click Save.

An offboard template: tick the actions, write the auto-reply, then save.

Save as new always creates a new template. To change one, select it and click Update.

Offboard actions you can turn on or off:

Action On by default Block sign-in Yes Hide from GAL Yes Mailbox auto-reply Yes Convert mailbox to shared Yes Grant mailbox Full Access (needs recipient) Yes Grant OneDrive edit access (needs recipient) Yes Remove group memberships (skip dynamic) Yes Remove Entra directory roles Yes Reassign direct reports (needs recipient) Yes Remove licenses last Yes Retire Intune devices (destructive) No

Actions marked "needs recipient" only run when the technician picks a handoff recipient on the Offboard page. Retire Intune devices also needs admin consent in the tenant. See Admin permissions.

docs.title: Create an onboard template
docs.text:
1. Open Templates and click Onboard, then New.
  2. Choose the optional steps: Assign licenses, Add to groups, Set manager. These always run: create user, set usage location, enable account, and force a password change at next sign-in.
  3. Set the Default usage location (two letters, for example US).
  4. Under Required fields, tick any extra fields the technician must fill in. Display name, usage location, and UPN are always required. Ticking Manager also turns on Set manager.
  5. Under Default groups & licenses, search for and add the groups and licenses every new hire should get.
  6. Click Save as new…, name it (for example "New hire — Sales"), and click Save.

An onboard template with three required fields, three default groups, and one license.

docs.title: Create a mover template
docs.text:
Mover templates describe the person's new role.

  1. Open Templates and click Mover, then New.
  2. Choose the steps: Update job profile, Set manager, Add to groups, Assign licenses.
  3. Fill in the Default new position fields you want preset.
  4. Add the groups and licenses the new role needs.
  5. Click Save as new… and name it.

docs.title: Use a template on a job
docs.text:
1. Open Offboard, Onboard, or Mover.
  2. In Template, pick the template and click Apply.
  3. Add the people and finish the job as usual. On Offboard, the Actions list is read-only and shows what the template turns on.

You can also select a template on Templates and click Apply to job. That opens the matching job page with the template applied.

When the label reads Template (required), you have to apply a template before Preview and Run unlock.

docs.title: Change or delete a template
docs.text: To Do this Change it Select it, edit, click Update, and confirm. This overwrites the saved template. Copy it Select it, edit, click Save as new…, and give it a new name. Delete it Select it and click the trash icon, then Remove.

docs.title: Set a default for the tenant
docs.text:
Select a template and click Set as default. The list then shows Default for tenant under its name, and jobs for that tenant start with it selected. Click Clear default to remove it.

Each tenant has its own default for each kind: one offboard, one onboard, and one mover template. Setting a mover default doesn't change the onboard default. When you're signed in to your YeetnGreet profile as an admin, the default is also shared with your techs.

A mover default. Mover jobs for Contoso start with Move to Sales selected.

docs.title: Publish a template to your team
docs.text:
A saved template lives on the PC where you saved it. To share it with your techs:

  1. Sign in to your YeetnGreet profile as an admin.
  2. Select the saved template.
  3. Click Publish at the top of the page.

Techs' PCs pull published templates and the tenant's default when they sign in to their YeetnGreet profile, and again when they open Tenants or Templates if the last pull is old. To pull immediately, they can open Settings → Profile → Refresh company catalog.

Publishing copies the template's settings to your YeetnGreet account: the actions, the auto-reply text, and the names and IDs of the groups and licenses in it. It doesn't copy any user data. Publish needs a paid plan.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Template Kind Settings Standard leaver Offboard Every action except Retire Intune devices. Auto-reply points to the manager. Immediate termination Offboard Same actions, but no auto-reply. New hire — Sales Onboard Business Premium, groups "All Staff" and "Sales Team". Job title, department, and manager required. Move to Sales Mover Update the job profile to Account Manager in Sales, and add the Sales Team and CRM Users groups.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Names are unique per kind and tenant. Saving a new template with a name that's already used fails. Use Update to change the existing one.
  • Templates are per tenant. Recreate or publish a template for each tenant that needs it.
  • Edit actions on Templates, not on the job page. The Offboard Actions list only shows what the applied template does.
  • Publish after you change a template. Your techs keep the last published version until you publish again.
  • Update overwrites the template right away. There's no version history, so copy it with Save as new… first if you might want the old settings back.

docs.title: Report delivery
docs.text:
Send license reports to the places your team already works: email, Teams, Slack, or your own automation.

Set it up in Reports → Report settings → Report delivery. Delivery settings are saved per tenant, and every channel is optional.

Turn on the channels you want, then click Save delivery config.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Channel What it does Email (Microsoft Graph) Sends the report files to the recipients you list. Needs an interactive sign-in. Not available in app-only mode. Microsoft Teams webhook Posts a notification to a Teams channel through an incoming webhook URL. Slack webhook Posts a notification to Slack through an incoming webhook URL. Generic webhook Sends a JSON payload to your HTTPS endpoint: {tenant, reportType, timestamp, status, files}.

Email sends several files as one ZIP. If the ZIP is bigger than the Max attachment size (3 MB by default, up to 10 MB), the email lists the local reports folder instead of attaching the files.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create the destination: a mailbox or distribution list, a Teams incoming webhook, a Slack incoming webhook, or an HTTPS listener.
  2. Open Reports → Report settings, expand the channel, tick Enable, and paste the address or URL.
  3. Click Save delivery config.
  4. Run a report once to check that it arrives, then add it to a schedule.

Keep webhook URLs private

Delivery settings stay on this PC. Anyone with a webhook URL can post to that channel, so store it like a password.

What-if exports are never delivered

What-if scenario exports are saved on this PC only. They are never emailed or posted, even when delivery is set up.

To see what gets delivered, download the sample reports.

docs.title: License audit
docs.text:
See which Microsoft 365 licenses are assigned — with SKU detail, mail activity (last 90 days), and attention rows for disabled + licensed and no mail users.

In the app this is the User licensing card on Reports after you run a license report.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Quarterly license hygiene
  • Before a renewal or true-up
  • After a merger / tenant consolidation wave
  • Finding named users to reclaim before you cut prepaid licenses

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the tenant and sign in
  2. Open Reports → Run license report
  3. Review the User licensing summary and table (filter by name, UPN, or license)
  4. Pair with What-if for priced reclaim and scenario planning
  5. Export or deliver as needed

The User licensing card lists the people who need attention, with their mail activity and licenses.

To see the exported report, download the sample license health report (PDF, HTML, and CSV, made with fictional data).

Plans

Free includes a limited license-report preview. Full named-user audit, exact savings, and exports are on paid plans. See Pricing and licensing.

Mail activity

No-mail detection needs Reports.Read.All. If mail metrics are missing, re-sign in to grant the permission — the app will not treat every licensed user as inactive when mail data did not load.

docs.title: Reports overview
docs.text: YeetnGreet reports help you see Microsoft 365 license waste from the same technician PC model as onboard/offboard jobs. You run Graph queries locally, then export or deliver results yourself.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text:
Report Purpose License audit Who is licensed, mail activity (90d), disabled+licensed and no-mail attention rows Unused licenses Unused prepaid licenses and licenses on disabled accounts What-if Reclaim savings and a scenario planner for moves, hires, and cuts Sample reports Download example exports made with fictional data

In the app these appear together on Reports after you run a license report — not as separate menu items.

docs.title: How to run
docs.text:
1. Select the managed tenant and sign in
  2. Open Reports → Run license report
  3. Review User licensing (audit) and What-if (reclaim + scenario planner)
  4. On the What-if card, type your own unit prices and click Save costs
  5. Optionally build a named scenario and export it to this PC, schedule a recurring report, or send the license report via Delivery

License audit: tenant totals up top, then every licensed user who needs attention — disabled + licensed or no mail in 90 days.

Plans

Free includes a limited license-report preview (bucketed savings, no SKU/$ detail or named users). Full SKU tables, exact savings, named users, scenario export, and deliveries are on paid plans. See Pricing and licensing.

Data path

Report queries use Microsoft Graph from the technician PC (Reports.Read.All for mail activity). Exports and delivery stay under your control — YeetnGreet does not host a data lake of customer report content. What-if scenarios are projections only; they never change licenses in the tenant, and scenario exports are saved on this PC only.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Pricing and licensing
  • Delivery

docs.title: Sample reports
docs.text:
These are real YeetnGreet exports, made with the app's own report templates from a fictional tenant. Download them to see exactly what you get. Your tenant names, licenses, and counts will differ.

Sample data only

Contoso, every person, and every address on contoso-example.com are made up. Each file carries a "Sample" label. The figures are a demo, not a promise of savings. Always check in your tenant before you remove licenses.

docs.title: License health report
docs.text:
The report you get from Reports → Run license report. It shows potential monthly savings, the license counts that matter, cost-saving opportunities for each license, and the named users who need attention.

Sample license health report: $428 a month in unused licenses and licenses on disabled accounts.

Download the sample:

  • License health report (PDF)
  • License health report (HTML)
  • Unused licenses (CSV): one row per license with unused and disabled counts and the monthly savings
  • Users needing attention (CSV): disabled but still licensed, or no mail in 90 days

What to look for:

  • Potential savings counts unused licenses and licenses on disabled accounts, times your unit price.
  • No mail (90d) users are listed for review but not counted in savings, because inactive doesn't always mean the license isn't needed.

docs.title: What-if scenario export
docs.text:
What you get when you click Export or Export PDF in the What-if scenario planner. This sample is the three-step plan from the What-if page: remove 7 unused Business Premium, move 10 people from E3 to Business Premium, and remove unused Business Basic (4 of the 10 asked for were unused).

Sample What-if export: −$318 a month (−$3,816 a year), and nothing changes in the tenant.

Download the sample:

  • What-if scenario (PDF)
  • What-if scenario (HTML)
  • What-if scenario (CSV): before and after counts and the monthly and yearly cost change for each license

The step list, the counts, and the costs all use what actually applied, so the export matches what you saw in the app. When a step was capped, the step shows both numbers, such as 4 of 10. A step that couldn't apply is marked as skipped, with the reason.

Scenario exports are saved on this PC only, in Documents\YeetnGreet\reports. They are never emailed or posted, and license assignments in the tenant stay the same.

docs.title: Unused licenses
docs.text:
Find prepaid licenses that are not assigned, and licenses still stuck on disabled accounts — before the renewal meeting.

In the app this is the Unused / Disabled columns on the license report’s What-if table (not a separate Reports submenu).

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Signal Meaning Unused Prepaid enabled licenses minus consumed (available capacity you are still paying for) Disabled License assignments on accounts with sign-in blocked No mail (90d) Enabled licensed users with no send/receive/read in the mail activity window — shown under User licensing for review. Not priced as reclaim because inactive is not confirmed waste.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Monthly license hygiene
  • After offboard waves (catch stragglers still licensed while disabled)
  • When finance asks “where can we cut?”

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the tenant and sign in
  2. Open Reports → Run license report
  3. On What-if, review Unused and Disabled per SKU
  4. Open User licensing for named disabled+licensed and no-mail users
  5. Validate in the Microsoft 365 admin center before you remove SKUs or reduce quantities
  6. Export or deliver if needed

Unused and Disabled columns per license, with the monthly savings for each.

User licensing names the people behind the numbers: disabled but still licensed, or no mail in 90 days.

Validate before reclaim

Unused and disabled signals are a starting point. Confirm with your process (shared mailboxes, break-glass accounts, seasonal staff) before you remove SKUs. Sample savings on the marketing site are examples only — not a guarantee.

docs.title: Pricing the reclaim
docs.text: Pair this view with What-if: set unit costs, then read Savings / mo for each license (unused plus disabled licenses, times the unit price). Use the scenario planner on the same card to model reclaim steps without changing the tenant.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• What-if
  • License audit
  • Sample reports

docs.title: What-if
docs.text:
Plan license changes before you make them in the admin center. What-if is on the Reports page, below User licensing, after you run a license report. It's read-only: nothing in the tenant changes.

The What-if savings card has two parts:

  1. Reclaim savings. What you could save on unused licenses and licenses still assigned to disabled accounts.
  2. Scenario planner. A named plan of steps with before and after license counts and the cost change.

docs.title: Reclaim savings
docs.text:
For each license, the table shows Enabled, Used, Unused, Disabled, the Unit / mo price, and Savings / mo.

  • Unused is licenses you pay for that nobody has.
  • Disabled is licenses still assigned to people whose sign-in is blocked.
  • Savings / mo is what those unused and disabled licenses cost each month.

Reclaim savings: $428 a month across unused and disabled licenses.

Inactive licensed users (no mail activity in 90 days) are listed under User licensing for review. They aren't counted in the savings, because inactive doesn't always mean the license isn't needed.

docs.title: Unit prices
docs.text:
Microsoft Graph doesn't report what you pay, so each license shows a price and where it came from:

Price source Meaning list-price estimate US list price. Used until you enter your own. enter cost A price you typed but haven't saved yet. saved tenant price A price you saved for this tenant with Save costs.

To use your own prices, type them in the Unit / mo column and click Save costs.

  • Only prices you type are saved. List-price estimates are never saved as your price.
  • $0 and blank are different. Type 0 for a license you get free, and it's saved as $0. Leave the box blank to use the list-price estimate. Clearing a saved price and saving again removes it.
  • If a license has no price at all, totals count it as $0 and the planner shows a warning.

Always check prices against your Microsoft bill before you make a decision.

docs.title: Scenario planner
docs.text:
1. Type a Scenario name, for example "Q4 reclaim + E3 to Business Premium".
  2. Pick a Step and a SKU, enter a Quantity, and click Add step. Repeat for each change.
  3. Read the before and after counts and the monthly and yearly change.
  4. Click Save to keep the scenario for this tenant.
Step What it does Quantity Remove unused licenses Stops paying for licenses nobody has Blank = all unused on that SKU Remove disabled-assigned licenses Removes licenses from disabled accounts and stops paying for them Blank = all on that SKU Move licenses (SKU → SKU) Moves people from one license to another, such as E3 to Business Premium. To can be a license the tenant doesn't have yet. Required Add licenses (planned hires) Adds licenses for new people Required Remove licenses (planned cuts) Removes licenses for planned reductions Required

A three-step scenario. The last step asked for 10 but only 4 were unused, so 4 were applied.

docs.title: How the cost is worked out
docs.text:
Each license's monthly cost is the number of licenses you pay for times its monthly unit price. The planner compares that before and after your steps.

Example: Business Premium at $22 and E3 at $36. The plan removes 5 unused Business Premium licenses, then moves 10 people from E3 to Business Premium. Before and after are license counts.

SKU Before After Monthly change Business Premium 50 55 +$110 E3 20 10 −$360

Total: −$250 a month (−$3,000 a year).

docs.title: When a step can't fully apply
docs.text:
• Capped step. If you ask for more than exist, the step applies what's available and says so, for example "Applied 4 of 10 — quantity capped to what is available."
  • Skipped step. If a step can't apply at all, it's shown in red with its step number and the reason, for example "Step 2 can't apply: Nothing to apply — that SKU has no matching licenses left." This usually happens when you open a scenario saved before a newer report. The totals leave that step out until you fix or remove it.
  • New steps are checked first. If a step you're adding can't apply, it isn't added, and the status bar says why.

A skipped step is named, and the totals leave it out until you fix or remove it.

docs.title: Save, open, and delete
docs.text:
• Save stores the scenario for the selected tenant on this PC.
  • Pick a scenario under Saved and click Open to load it. Its steps are recalculated against the latest report.
  • Delete removes the selected saved scenario. You're asked to confirm first.
  • New starts an empty scenario.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
• Export saves an HTML report and a CSV. Export PDF also saves a PDF.
  • Files go to Documents\YeetnGreet\reports on this PC, and the HTML report opens in your browser.
  • Exporting never emails or posts the scenario, even if the tenant has report delivery set up. Share the files yourself.
  • The export lists each step with the quantity that applied. A capped step shows both numbers, such as 4 of 10.
  • Fix or remove any skipped step before you export.
  • See a sample What-if export (PDF, HTML, and CSV).

Name scenarios clearly

A name like "Q4 reclaim + E3 to Business Premium" makes it easy for the next person to find and reuse.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the tenant and sign in on Tenants.
  2. Open Reports and click Run license report.
  3. In What-if savings, check the unit prices, type your own where you have them, and click Save costs.
  4. In Scenario planner, add steps, review the totals, and click Save.
  5. Optionally click Export or Export PDF.

The Free plan shows a savings range without per-license prices, named users, or scenario export.

docs.text: Optional hybrid Active Directory support can be enabled per tenant when an organization needs on-prem identity alongside Entra ID.

  • Offboard and onboard paths that must respect on-prem + cloud steps your team defines

docs.title: How to think about it
docs.text:
Topic Guidance Scope Optional per managed tenant — enable only where needed Where it runs Still on the technician PC model; not “upload AD to YeetnGreet cloud” Availability Hybrid support is planned; pricing follows the same licensed-user bands on the pricing page

Cloud-only tenants

If a tenant is cloud-only Entra, you can ignore hybrid settings entirely.

docs.title: Multi-tenant
docs.text: Switch between the Microsoft 365 tenants on your account without mixing up context — as long as you confirm the active tenant before Live work. Licensed users are pooled across all tenants on the account for billing.

docs.title: Switching tenants
docs.text:
1. Open the tenant switcher in YeetnGreet
  2. Select the tenant you are about to work on
  3. Confirm domain / display name matches the ticket
  4. Continue with onboard, offboard, or reports

The tenant switcher in the left rail. Every job and report runs against the tenant shown here.

Wrong-tenant rule

Preview and type-to-confirm protect actions, but they do not fix picking the wrong organization. Habit: read the tenant name before every confirm.

docs.text:
Plan Managed tenants Free 1 Paid plans (Starter and above) Multiple tenants; licensed users pooled across the account

See Pricing and licensing for licensed-user bands and prices.
